regulatory_basis: Section 12, Prevention of Money-Laundering Act, 2002 r/w Rule 3, PML (Maintenance of Records) Rules, 2005 - reported to FIU-IND
recommended_action: Escalate to compliance officer the same business day
narrative: Account UTIB119613 has been assessed as HIGH risk. Over the observation window it received Rs 1,237,650 and disbursed Rs 490,000. The account was surfaced by 2 independent detection layer(s) evidencing network chokepoint, pass-through conduit. The account does not act alone: it is one of 7 accounts in RING-01, alongside CNRB243795, HDFC259211, HDFC801992, ICIC176070, ICIC511423, PUNB549145, moving Rs 5,257,409 between themselves. Taken together the transaction pattern has no apparent lawful or economic purpose and is consistent with the placement and layering of proceeds of crime. A Suspicious Transaction Report is warranted under Section 12 of the Prevention of Money-Laundering Act, 2002 read with Rule 3 of the PML (Maintenance of Records) Rules, 2005.

grounds_of_suspicion.detail: Received Rs 500,000 from UTIB165839 on day 18 and forwarded Rs 490,000 to HDFC259211 on day 19 - 98.0% passed on, 2.0% skimmed, held 1 day(s). The account stores no value; it is a conduit, which is the defining signature of a money mule. It is not a settlement rail: the behaviour occurs 1 time(s), not on a recurring schedule.

Chokepoint of the suspicious sub-network: betweenness 0.0061, +2.4 standard deviations above the other alerted accounts. A disproportionate share of criminal payment paths runs through this single account, so an account freeze here fragments the network rather than displacing it. Corroborates the primary flag; does not create it.

action_taken: Sub-network temporary hold recommended; account and its one-hop neighbourhood quarantined pending FIU-IND acknowledgement.
